chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man: is it proper for him to look at his wife when she dies, or to perform ghusl for her if there is no one with her to perform ghusl for her? And about the woman: may she look at the like of that from her husband when he dies?
He عليه السلام said: There is no harm in that. Rather, the woman's family only does that out of dislike that her husband should look at something of her that they dislike.

key_terms.حِينَ تَمُوتُ: at the time when she dies
key_terms.حِينَ يَمُوتُ: at the time when he dies
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.يُغَسِّلَهَا: to perform the ritual washing of the deceased woman

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife perform ghusl for their spouse after death in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that there is no objection to a husband looking at or performing ghusl for his wife after her death, and likewise for a wife with her husband. It also notes that when the woman's family undertakes this, it is due to their own dislike of the husband seeing something they would dislike from her.
